rows.title: A little change is good
rows.body: You may notice things are changing a bit around here. Take a look around. We are trying to focus on our core mission of appreciating nature: signs on the plants, displays in our air conditioned spaces, interesting facts about all the species here. More to come, so stay tuned!

rows.title: Help keep Palma Sola growing
rows.body: Membership supports the gardens you’re enjoying today. Join at the office — it takes about two minutes.
rows.link_text: Stop by the office on your way out

rows.title: Take a plant home
rows.body: Shop the nursery Tuesday and Saturday mornings. Plants are propagated here or donated by community friends — and every sale supports the park.
rows.link_text: Nursery is by the back gate

rows.title: Take your wedding vows right here
rows.body: The Galleria and the deck host weddings, showers, memorials and company dinners — surrounded by ten acres of garden.
rows.link_text: Ask about dates at the office

rows.title: Remembering Ina Baden
rows.body: Ina Baden was part of Palma Sola for many years, helping run the park office and sharing in the growth of the gardens we know today. We were grateful to gather with her family and friends here at the park on September 20 to remember and celebrate her life. She remains very much in our thoughts.

rows.title: The Galleria is available
rows.body: The Galleria seats a crowd for classes, meetings, dinners and celebrations.

rows.title: Scan the plants signs
rows.body: New signs are going up across the park this month. Scan the code with your phone to discover what's growing here.
rows.link_text: Look for them on the metal posts

rows.title: Your photo could be here next
rows.body: Every photo in our plant and wildlife catalog came from our community. Post to iNaturalist at Palma Sola — yours could be next, credited to you.
rows.link_text: Ask us how to get started

rows.title: Thank you, Selby Foundation
rows.body: New tables. New chairs. More ways to gather. A $20,000 gift from the William G. & Marie Selby Foundation is helping refresh our Galleria.

rows.title: Thank you, Bishop Parker Foundation
rows.body: The gathering deck was rebuilt in lasting composite — ready for years of weddings, classes and quiet moments by the pond.

rows.title: The Butterfly Garden is that way
rows.body: Karen planted it and still tends it. Best light is mid-morning, and the zebra longwings are usually the first to show up.
rows.link_text: Follow the path past the Galleria

rows.title: New Deck Completed!
rows.body: Thanks to the Bishop Parker Foundation, our beautiful new composite deck is finished just in time for the season.

rows.title: It is hot. Drink something.
rows.body: Water is available at the office. Shade is easiest to find along the Rare Fruit Trail and under the big oaks.

rows.title: June 2026 Newsletter
rows.body: Yes, the newsletter is not just for your inbox anymore!  Come read it online.

rows.title: Park closed December 17–20
rows.body: Winter Nights under the Lights takes over the whole park those evenings. Plan your visit around it — or come to the event.

rows.title: We could use the help
rows.body: Adult workdays, the nursery crew, the butterfly garden, irrigation, events. No experience needed and the coffee is free.
rows.link_text: Ask at the office how to join a workday

rows.title: Six places worth wandering
rows.body: The Rare Fruit Trail, Palm Alley, the Butterfly Garden, the Serenity Garden, the big pond and the boardwalk. None of them take long.
rows.link_text: Grab a map at the office

rows.title: This park is free. Every day.
rows.body: Ten acres, open 365 days a year, no admission. Kept that way by members, donors and a lot of volunteer muscle.
rows.link_text: Ask at the office about becoming a member
